Welcome toParrett and Axe CE VA Primary School
Hello and welcome to Parrett and Axe CE VA Primary School! On behalf of all our children and staff, I’d like to say how delighted we are that you’ve stopped by to find out more about our school.
We’re a small, friendly village school set in the beautiful West Dorset countryside, and we’re proud of the caring, family feel that makes our school such a special place to learn and grow. Read More
"Love your neighbour as yourself" (Luke 10 vs 27)
We are very proud of our latest OFSTED Inspection. To read the report please click here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Parrett & Axe CE VA Primary School - French
pageCache.text:
french
At Parrett and Axe CE VA Primary School, we want every child to enjoy learning languages and feel confident as young linguists. In Key Stage Two, we teach French through fun and engaging lessons where children get plenty of opportunities to listen, speak, read, and start writing in French.
Our aim is to spark curiosity, build confidence, and give pupils a strong foundation for language learning as they move on to secondary school. We follow the PlanIt Scheme, which uses exciting topics and a clear sequence of lessons to make sure skills develop step by step and children build on what they’ve learned each year.
French 2 Year Rolling Curriculum
KS2 French Curriculum Progression Map
This French progression map supports practitioners using the PlanIt scheme (in part or in full) to deliver a high-quality Modern Foreign Languages curriculum. It sets out a clear sequence of skills and knowledge from Year 3 to Year 6, ensuring pupils meet and exceed the National Curriculum expectations for Key Stage 2 languages.
KS2 National Curriculum Expectations
By the end of KS2, pupils will be taught to:
Listen attentively to spoken French and respond appropriately.
Explore language patterns and sounds through songs, rhymes, and stories, linking spelling, sound, and meaning.
Engage in conversations, ask and answer questions, and express opinions, seeking clarification when needed.
Speak in sentences using familiar vocabulary, phrases, and structures.
Develop accurate pronunciation and intonation when speaking and reading aloud.
Present ideas and information orally to a range of audiences.
Read carefully, showing understanding of words, phrases, and simple texts.
Write phrases and sentences from memory, adapting these to create new ideas.
Broaden vocabulary, use dictionaries, and understand basic grammar, including gender, verb conjugation, and sentence structure.
Appreciate French stories, songs, poems, and rhymes.

Music
Music Development Plan – 2024–25 (Summary)
Music at Parrett and Axe inspires creativity, confidence, and cultural awareness. It provides every child with opportunities to perform, compose, and appreciate music from a wide range of traditions. Music is central to our school community, enriching learning and fostering self-expression, teamwork, and resilience.
Key Features of High-Quality Music Provision
Weekly music lessons (1+ hour) across all key stages.
Access to instrumental/vocal lessons and music technology.
Choir/ensemble opportunities and termly performances.
Adequate practice and rehearsal spaces.
Live music experiences annually.
Curriculum aligns with National Plan for Music Education and Model Music Curriculum.
Development Priorities 2024–25
1. Strengthen delivery of weekly music lessons (Charanga).
Inconsistent confidence; progression not always clear.
High-quality weekly lessons taught confidently by all staff.

2. Improve assessment and monitoring of progress.
Enrichment well-evidenced; lesson progress less tracked.

- Create class music folders.- Collect annotated planning and lesson evidence.- Termly monitoring by subject lead.
Staff time; shared drives.
3. Expand and refresh school music resources.
Limited, outdated instruments.
Broad range of quality resources accessible to all pupils.
- Fundraise for KS2 recorders.- Acquire tuned/untuned instruments.- Hire ukuleles from Music Hub.

Share plan with Dorset Music Hub for targeted support.
Monitor and review progress termly.
Build a vibrant, inclusive music culture central to school life.

pageCache.pageTitle: Parrett & Axe CE VA Primary School - English
pageCache.text:
English
Our Intent At Parrett and Axe CE VA Primary School, we are committed to ensuring that every pupil receives high-quality teaching in English from the moment they join us until the day they leave. Our approach combines a rigorous and effective phonics programme with a rich, immersive, topic-based curriculum to foster a love of language and communication.
Reading Our intent is for all pupils to become confident, fluent, and enthusiastic readers who read widely and with understanding. We achieve this through high-quality guided reading sessions, exposure to a diverse selection of fiction and non-fiction texts, and the promotion of a strong culture of reading across the school.
Writing We are dedicated to developing pupils’ writing skills progressively, building knowledge and confidence year on year. Through our topic-based curriculum, children write with depth and purpose across a range of subjects and genres, while also expanding their vocabulary and refining their style. We provide meaningful and enriching opportunities for writing, ensuring every child has a real-life purpose for their work. Regardless of starting points, we aim for all pupils to leave our school as skilled, confident communicators, fully prepared for the next stage of their education.

pageCache.pageTitle: Parrett & Axe CE VA Primary School - Mathematics

Mathematics
Our Intent
At Parrett and Axe CE VA Primary school, we work tirelessly to ensure that, from the day they arrive to the day they leave, giving all pupils access to equitable classrooms; classrooms where pupils can all participate and be influential, and classrooms where pupils are encouraged and supported to develop a deep, connected and sustained understanding of the mathematics being explored. This reflects our approach to Mastery Maths. To achieve this, our efforts are focused on problem solving, reasoning and investigation-based learning through the use of concrete, pictorial and abstract approaches throughout the school.
We strive for all learners to have opportunities to be immersed in and engaged with meaningful mathematical activities which build on prior learning and understanding, focus on relational understanding and encourage persistence and resilience in all aspects of school life.
We aim for every pupil to leave with the necessary skills and confidence to independently apply deep mathematical understanding in a wide range of contexts which will enable them to make at least good progress at secondary school and beyond.

PSHE
At Parrett and Axe CE VA Primary School, we deliver a comprehensive and progressive PSHE and wellbeing curriculum through the SCARF programme, developed by Coram Life Education. SCARF – which stands for Safety, Caring, Achievement, Resilience, and Friendship – provides a structured, age-appropriate framework that promotes pupils’ emotional health, wellbeing, and personal development. pageCache.pageTitle: Parrett & Axe CE VA Primary School - RE
pageCache.text:
RE
Intent
At Parrett and Axe CE VA Primary School, our intent is to nurture every child’s spiritual growth, helping them to develop self-awareness, empathy, and a reflective approach to life. All that we do is rooted in our core Christian values of Kindness, Courage, Respect, and Equality, which are taught in the context of Christian beliefs and practice and supported by Understanding Christianity.
We are committed to fostering the spiritual, emotional, moral, social, cultural, physical, and academic development of each unique child, enabling them to experience life in all its fullness. Through their RE learning, pupils are taught to be compassionate, caring, and reflective, inspired by the Biblical teaching:
“Love your neighbour as yourself.” (Luke 10:27)
Our RE curriculum is designed to give pupils a deep understanding of Christianity alongside knowledge of other world faiths and worldviews. It aims to help children become thoughtful, informed, and respectful individuals, able to explore life’s big questions and reflect on their own values and beliefs.
We focus on three key strands of knowledge:
Substantive Knowledge – Core content, concepts, and vocabulary about religious and non-religious beliefs and practices.
Disciplinary Knowledge – How we study religion, developing enquiry, interpretation, and evaluation skills.
Personal Knowledge – Encouraging self-awareness and reflection on personal values, beliefs, and assumptions.
Our aim is for all pupils to leave Parrett and Axe:
Knowledgeable and curious about a range of religions and worldviews.
Respectful and empathetic towards others with different beliefs.
Equipped with critical thinking skills to engage thoughtfully with religious and philosophical questions.
Implementation
Our RE curriculum is based on the Dorset Agreed Syllabus and enriched through Understanding Christianity and Discovery RE materials, which provide a coherent and progressive framework.
Key features include:
Early Years: Pupils begin learning about celebrations and festivals, comparing similarities and differences between their own experiences and those of others. They retell stories through play, role-play, and storytelling, with observations recorded in Tapestry to track understanding.
Key Stage 1 and 2: Pupils follow a two-year rolling programme that develops depth and progression. Christianity is taught as a spiral theme, interwoven with studies of other major world religions to build a broad understanding of global diversity. Lessons include enquiry-based learning, artefacts, digital resources, and collaborative activities.
Community Links: We maintain strong partnerships with local churches, including Mosterton Church and Beaminster Churches, led by Revd David Baldwin. Children regularly participate in church services, faith team meetings, and classroom sessions enriched by church leaders.
Teaching and Assessment: Teachers creatively adapt plans to meet class needs, ensuring lessons are practical and engaging. RE books/folders, pupil voice, and book studies are used to assess knowledge retention, progression, and to strengthen long-term memory.
Through this approach, children are encouraged to:
Ask meaningful and challenging questions.
Use precise religious vocabulary confidently.
Express their own views respectfully and listen to those of others.
Impact
By the time they leave Parrett and Axe, pupils will:
Describe and make meaningful connections between religious and non-religious beliefs and practices.
Recognise and explain links between stories, traditions, and actions in faith communities.
Explore and evaluate beliefs, values, and practices with curiosity and empathy.
Appreciate diversity and understand the importance of mutual respect in a multi-faith world.
Discuss and present thoughtful views on religion, faith, and morality.
Understand the challenges of faith and commitment and its impact on community life.
Our RE curriculum equips pupils with knowledge, critical thinking skills, and respect for diversity, empowering them to become thoughtful, compassionate members of society who are confident in navigating life’s big questions.

pageCache.pageTitle: Parrett & Axe CE VA Primary School - PE & Sports Premium
pageCache.text:
PE & Sports Premium
Physical Education (PE)
At Parrett & Axe, we believe PE is an essential part of every child’s education. Through a broad and balanced curriculum, we aim to help pupils develop not only physical skills but also teamwork, confidence, and a lifelong love of movement.
Our Approach
Curriculum PE: All pupils take part in weekly PE lessons covering a range of sports, games, dance, gymnastics, and athletics.
Specialist Coaches: To enrich our provision, we work with qualified external coaches who bring specialist knowledge and expertise. This allows children to experience a variety of sports and learn new skills in an engaging way.
Staff Collaboration: Our teachers work alongside coaches to ensure that sessions are tailored to meet the needs of every pupil and build progression across year groups.
Inclusive for All: Every child is encouraged to participate and succeed, regardless of ability or experience.
Opportunities Beyond Lessons
Clubs & Enrichment: We offer a range of after-school sports clubs run by our coaches and staff.
Competitions & Festivals: Children are given the chance to represent the school in local sporting events, fostering teamwork, resilience, and school spirit.
Healthy Lifestyle: Through PE and sport, we promote the importance of staying active and making healthy choices.
PE Lessons
KS2 PE lessons: Tuesdays
On these days, pupils should attend school in their full PE kit.
KS1 PE lessons: Thursdays
Sports Premium Grant
At Parrett & Axe, we are committed to ensuring that every pupil has access to high-quality Physical Education, school sport and opportunities for physical activity. The PE and Sports Premium Grant is additional funding provided by the Government to improve the quality and breadth of PE and sport provision in primary schools.
Purpose of the Funding
The PE and Sports Premium must be used to make additional and sustainable improvements to the quality of PE, physical activity and sport across the school. At Parrett & Axe, we use the funding to:
Develop staff expertise through training and professional development, ensuring high-quality teaching of PE across the curriculum.
Work with specialist coaches to provide pupils with expert teaching and access to a wider range of sports.
Increase participation in extracurricular clubs and sporting competitions.
Promote physical activity and healthy lifestyles for all pupils, encouraging lifelong habits that support well-being.
Improve resources and equipment to enhance the delivery of PE and active playtimes.
Accountability and Impact
Schools are required to publish details of how the Sports Premium is spent and the impact it has on pupils’ physical activity and sport participation. At Parrett & Axe, we evaluate our provision regularly to ensure the funding:
raises the profile of PE and sport across the school;
engages all pupils in regular physical activity;
develops confidence, resilience and social skills through competitive sport and teamwork;
has a lasting impact by building staff expertise and sustainable practices.
Annual Reports
Each year, we publish a breakdown of our Sports Premium spending and an evaluation of the impact on pupils. You can read our latest report here.

Applying Technology – Learning how to use a wide range of digital tools for communication, creativity, data handling, modelling, and multimedia.

Each area is further broken down into clear strands, enabling progressive skill development:

pageCache.text:
After-School Clubs
Our after-school clubs provide pupils with opportunities to explore new skills, make friends, and have fun in a supportive and engaging environment.
We offer a variety of clubs to suit different interests and talents, including:
Hockey Club (KS2) – Develop teamwork, coordination, and ball skills while learning the fundamentals of hockey in a friendly and inclusive setting.
Drama Club (Y1-Y6) – Express creativity, boost confidence, and explore performance through acting, improvisation, and storytelling activities.
Cross Country Club (KS2) – Build stamina, resilience, and a love of running with exciting challenges for all abilities.
Girls Football Club (KS2) – Encourage teamwork, fitness, and ball skills in a safe, enjoyable environment, celebrating sportsmanship and participation.
Clubs run on different days throughout the week and are led by our dedicated teachers and coaches. They are open to all pupils, regardless of previous experience, and are a fantastic way to make the most of the school day while discovering new passions.
We encourage all pupils to try something new and enjoy the chance to learn, play, and grow beyond the classroom. Keep an eye on our school newsletter for the latest club schedules and sign-up information.

pageCache.pageTitle: Parrett & Axe CE VA Primary School - Tapestry
pageCache.text:
At Parrett & Axe we use Tapestry, a secure online learning journal, to record and share the experiences, progress, and achievements of our youngest learners during their time in Corfe Class.
What is Tapestry?
Tapestry is an interactive platform used primarily in the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS). It allows teachers and parents to build a rich picture of each child’s learning journey through photos, videos, and written observations.
How We Use Tapestry
In School: Staff capture special moments of learning, play, and progress in the classroom and outdoors. These observations are linked to the Early Years curriculum so that we can track development in all key areas.
At Home: Parents and carers can log in securely to see what their child has been learning, celebrate achievements, and even add their own observations from home. This helps create a strong partnership between school and families.
Together: Sharing learning in this way encourages children to talk about their activities at home and builds a sense of pride and confidence in their progress.
Benefits of Tapestry
Provides parents with regular insights into their child’s learning.
Encourages strong home–school links, with parents actively contributing to their child’s learning journal.
Creates a complete record of development during the early years of school.
Secure and password-protected, ensuring children’s data is safe.
Getting Started
Parents are provided with a secure log-in when their child joins our EYFS class. Tapestry can be accessed through the website or via the free app (available on iOS and Android). If you need support accessing Tapestry, please speak to your child’s teacher or the school office.
